subject: Add master key primitives for machine-bound connection files
body:
Add master key primitives for machine-bound connection files

First step toward keying connection files to the machine instead of the
hardcoded "mR3m" default: the key material and the keyed cipher path. Nothing
reads or writes connection files differently yet, so this changes no behaviour.

Secrets are currently encrypted one field at a time, each with its own random
salt, so PBKDF2 runs once per secret rather than once per file. That is why the
iteration count sits at 10,000: raising it to current guidance (600k) would cost
roughly a minute of PBKDF2 per load on a 100-connection file. A random master key
removes the per-field derivation entirely, which is what makes strong protection
affordable here.

- MasterKey: random 256-bit key, sized for AES-GCM, with best-effort zeroing.
- DpapiMasterKeyProtector: wraps that key with DPAPI CurrentUser, so a copied
  file cannot be read by another Windows account or machine. CurrentUser rather
  than LocalMachine, which would expose every credential to any local account.
- AeadCryptographyProvider.EncryptWithKey/DecryptWithKey: encrypt with an
  already-derived key. Output omits the salt, so it is deliberately not
  interchangeable with the password form; the file will record which is in use.

Tests cover round-trips, wrong keys, tampering, nonce reuse, unicode, and that
the two ciphertext formats cannot be confused for each other.

Gate CI on the security tests only: the full suite is 84/2099 red and was
already so before these changes, verified against a baseline build.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
